_about: Opinions and estimates about the family members, written by hand and labelled. FACTS (HEAD, dates, licence, privacy, Pages, CI conclusion) are NOT kept here: tools/family/family-index.mjs reads them from the GitHub API and local clones and writes MANIFEST.json. Completion figures are the 2026-10-26 measured review's estimate toward each repo's OWN definition of done (REVIEW_2026-10-26.md); they are not a grade and not a promise.

aster.name: Aster
aster.role: MEMBER + HUB (product: Lens L1 Transit shipped; P0 aster-mcp founded but broken at HEAD)
aster.one_liner: Browser-based asteroid mission planner with evidence-carrying answers: a 41,906-body NEA catalog, Lambert/porkchop/ΔV/DLA screening, and an MCP server that refuses with a reason when a question is out of envelope.

completion.label: [Likely]
completion.basis: Product-vision v1 (Slices 10-14) met mid-2026; 97/97 test files and a byte-identical rebuild measured 2026-10-26; held below 100 because the agent surface (mcp/) has not compiled since 2026-10-14 and the published package lags the site on disclosures. Against Slice 19.5's own exit the figure is ~30.

aster.verdict: The one repo with a real, reproducible product whose core claim, one core two interfaces, is false today on the interface agents consume. Fix mcp/ and put it in CI before any family work touches it.
aster.proves: node tools/run-tests.mjs · npx tsc --noEmit · CI: tsc, build, golden numbers, full-tests
aster.since: Mar 2026 (V1) · V2 from Apr 2026 · main history rewritten 2026-10-12
aster.note: MIT, but the LICENSE file wraps the text in prose so GitHub reports NOASSERTION. Founding docs are additive-only; src/v2/core is a protected math surface. Slice 16 agent-honesty study is pre-registered (Zenodo DOI) and its promised REPORT.md is still owed.

skyhook.name: Skyhook
skyhook.role: MEMBER (Works: the physical program; Lens L9 Momentum is the planning lens over it, not a rename of it)
skyhook.one_liner: Phase 0 study of a rotating momentum-exchange tether in a 610 km orbit. Rev A (2.5 km/s tip) is canonical in params/rev_a.json; a tested Python finance model prices the program honestly, including the conservative case that does not close.

completion.label: [Likely]
completion.basis: Against the repo's own Phase 0 exit (twin validated against flight data, joint statistics, capture demo): zero physical data. As a self-consistent paper study it is ~65% on main (73 passed / 1 skipped measured 2026-10-26), ~75% with the six unmerged agent branches.

skyhook.verdict: The deepest physics in the family, resting on an un-spot-checked materials assumption (HMPE creep at SF 2.5) and a remote that has outrun the repo's own single-source-of-truth rule: 46 agent commits on six branches no file mentions. Reconcile, then run the $120 splice test before writing another finance module.
skyhook.proves: python3 -m pytest tests/ -v · python3 physics/skyhook_physics.py · CI: Rev A physics assertions (main only)
skyhook.note: Private, no LICENSE, Pages off. params/rev_a.json disagrees with itself on Earth radius (com_radius_km 6988 vs the 6371 the physics module uses). The weakest input is named in the data: fiber_cost_per_kg is null.

partforge.name: PartForge
partforge.role: MEMBER (Works: fabrication tool and the family's measurement authority)
partforge.one_liner: Describe a part, get a printable parametric OpenSCAD model compiled in the browser. Flight grade turns the same tool on rocket-club machined parts: declared tolerances, a mesh CMM, engineering checks, and documents that say who stands behind every number.

completion.label: [Speculative]
completion.basis: The repo never defines done. Every re-runnable software claim matched (733 + 20 + 27 checks; 21/21 headless parity) but zero parts have ever been cut, the shipped flight template is 100% tool-default tolerances, roadmap items #3-#5 are unbuilt, and there is no CI.

partforge.verdict: A genuinely good idea (declare, measure, provenance, refuse) implemented as a 1.24 MB single HTML file that has never touched metal; it changes category from self-consistent to validated the day one centering ring is cut and calipered.
partforge.proves: node tests/run.mjs · cd headless && npm run test:parity
partforge.note: Apache-2.0. Pushes every commit straight to the Pages-served main with no CI; one deploy failed silently on 2026-10-05. Two pinned headless dependencies carry HIGH advisories. 85 of 94 commits are agent-authored and nothing in the repo says so.

ideabank.name: Idea-Bank
ideabank.role: LAB (sandbox: linked from the family, disclosed and licensed, otherwise frozen at 75)
ideabank.one_liner: Seventy-five side projects that AI agents chose, built, tested and graded themselves, each with an honest assessment. Several are orbital-mechanics explorables or printable space objects (a Kirkwood-gap ruler, Kepler gears, a reaction-wheel simulator).

completion.label: [Likely]
completion.basis: Per-deposit contract met for 75/75 when run uncontended (1,161 node tests, 108 Python, 148/148 phone+desktop smoke, 11/11 STLs). Withheld: no LICENSE, no CI, no pinned dependencies, 37 of 75 ideas never independently reviewed, and 30 review commits that now point at the wrong idea numbers.

ideabank.verdict: The fastest-moving and most phone-tested surface in the family, with the weakest audit trail; a LICENSE, a one-job CI and a PROCESS.md turn a three-day sprint into a bank others can withdraw from.
ideabank.proves: node tools/check.mjs · node tools/smoke.mjs <idea> · python3 tools/printcheck.py <idea>
ideabank.note: No LICENSE, no CI. 98 of 108 commits are agent-authored; the 'Made by' names are agent personas and the README does not yet say so. Nothing has been printed or played by two people.

suborbital.name: suborbital-leg-cost-model
suborbital.role: ARCHIVED (recommended: one pointer commit, then GitHub archive)
suborbital.one_liner: A one-commit stub from 2026-07-07. Its mandate (procure-vs-develop for the Skyhook suborbital leg, with sourced provider pricing) was folded back into the skyhook repo the same day and is itself still half-done there.

completion.label: [Certain]
completion.basis: Seven files, 134 lines, no code, no data, no sourced price; skyhook/docs/providers/README.md records the fold-back.

suborbital.verdict: An honest, well-formed stub that is now an attractive nuisance: its STATUS still tells a reader to start work here. Archive with a forward pointer; carry its decision-record template to skyhook; finish its job inside skyhook.
suborbital.note: Private, no LICENSE. Its only unique content is docs/decisions/TEMPLATE.md (DRAFT → PROPOSED → LOCKED), used by no other repo.

edges.text: Kernel K2: is a returning payload's Earth-arrival v∞ inside the Rev A tether's catch envelope? A research prototype exists on branch claude/k2-momentum-bank (tools/k2-momentum-research/); it snapshots params/rev_a.json with its sha256 and a verify gate reproduces Rev A's derived numbers (the live file still matches, read 2026-10-26). PR #1 for that branch has been open since 2026-10-06. Blocked on K1, the return-leg porkchop, which Aster does not have. [Certain the files exist · Likely on the findings]

PM-001 on skyhook's unmerged branch claude/skyhook-fixes-2026-10-22 freezes aster-mission-mcp@0.1.0 tool results into a data file. Note the trap: 0.1.0 lacks the fidelity tiers the web app shows. [Certain per the verified card]
Folded back on 2026-07-07; the leg-cost model lives in skyhook/finance/leg_cost.py, with its procure anchor still an unsourced $15M constant. [Certain]

Seven ideas ship eleven STL files and a print check (tools/printcheck.py). PartForge is the family's printability and measurement authority. No code link today. [Certain: no link exists · Speculative: worth one]
The ST-001 splice field kit is a physical test rig; PartForge Flight grade could declare and measure a printed gauge clip for it (never the load-bearing capstan drum). No link today. [Speculative]
